name: National Merit Scholarship Program

Roughly 1.5 million entrants per year. Also consider Alternate Entry only if no qualifying PSAT is possible.

name: Yale Model Congress (YMC)

notes: YMC 2026: Dec 3-6, 2026, New Haven, CT; registration opens Sept 1, 2026; delegation fees due by Oct 6, 2026 (late fee $50 after); financial aid decisions ~mid-Oct; committee placements in October. Includes Yale Day with faculty talks; 4 current Supreme Court justices are Yale alumni.

name: Close Up Washington, D.C. High School Programs
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12) participating via a school group or delegation

name: ACLU National Advocacy Institute: Washington, D.C.
eligibility: High school students ages 15-18 enrolled in a U.S. high school

aid: Need-based tuition assistance and travel stipends

Participants lobby Congress on issues like immigration and free speech.

Committees include House, Senate, Supreme Court, cabinet, and press corps; 40 committees; 9:1 delegate-to-staffer ratio; 250+ scholarships. Registration via school delegation; check harvardmodelcongress.org/boston for 2027 dates and fees.

name: Profile in Courage Essay Contest (JFK Library)
eligibility: U.S. high school students in grades 9-12 attending public, private, parochial, or home school; U.S. students under 20 in correspondence/GED programs; U.S. citizens attending school overseas.

name: Prudential Emerging Visionaries
eligibility: Ages 14-18 at application and not older than 18 by the end of the entry period; legal residents of the U.S. or Puerto Rico; must be leading an ongoing project/initiative that addresses a financial or societal challenge (project started on or before June 1 of the entry year).

notes: Applications are submitted through the Ashoka Changemakers platform. Judged on innovation, potential to scale, and community impact; winners announced in early 2027 with a summit in spring. Formerly the Prudential Spirit of Community Awards.; [DEAD: https://www.prudential.com/emerging-visionaries]

name: Connecticut Bar Foundation - Quintin Johnstone Statewide High School Essay Contest
eligibility: All Connecticut students under 21 enrolled in grades 9-12 at an accredited Connecticut high school, vocational-technical school, or adult high school credit diploma program; Connecticut homeschooled students in grades 9-12 also eligible.
cost: Free to apply
aid: $2,000 for winners; $1,000 for runners-up
notes: Sponsored by the Connecticut Bar Foundation's James W. Cooper Fellows. The 2025-26 contest deadline was February 20, 2026; the next cycle deadline is expected around February 2027. Essays judged on content/originality, organization, use of resource materials, and writing; topic changes annually (2025-26: education policy in the wake of Mahmoud v. Taylor).

name: Indiaspora Heritage Connect
eligibility: High school juniors or seniors of Indian origin (Indian diaspora) between the ages of 17 and 19, from the U.S., Canada, U.K., UAE, Singapore, or Australia.
cost: Free to apply (program fully funded for selected participants)

notes: Run by Indiaspora, a nonprofit network of prominent Indian diaspora leaders. Two-part application: an online Google Form plus a program application emailed to heritageconnect@indiaspora.org. The 2026 edition (announced August 2026) selects a small cohort (earlier editions took ~8 students); also a strong identity/leadership item for college applications. Check indiaspora.org for the current window.

name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
eligibility: US high school students in grades 9-12; register only through a school that has registered and paid the $125 fee
cost: $125 per school (covers all participating students); no per-student fee
aid: None
notes: 2027 cycle: school registration and $125 fee payment due by Oct 23, 2026; student registration deadline Nov 15, 2026 (registration opened Aug 7, 2026). Open Exam administered at school in early February 2027 (Feb 3, 2027 per 2027-cycle listings; official calendar at usabo-trc.org), Semifinal ~March 2027, Finals ~May-June 2027. IBO 2027 in Warsaw, Poland, July 18-25. No individual registration - confirm your school's test administrator registers. Prep resources on the Student Resource Center after school fee is paid; past exams available.

name: AMC 10/12 (American Mathematics Competitions) and AIME
eligibility: AMC 12: students in grade 12 or below, under 19.5 on contest day; AMC 10: grade 10 or below, under 17.5

aid: None

Regular registration deadline for new competition managers Oct 15, 2026; late deadline (returning managers only) Oct 28, 2026. AIME I/II dates TBD, expected February 2027. You may take both A and B sittings; higher score counts for AIME qualification. Free prep: MAA past exams and AoPS archives.

name: Science Olympiad (Division C)
eligibility: US high school students grades 9-12 via school teams (Division C; max 15 roster members, max 7 twelfth-graders)
cost: National rules and resources free; state/regional tournament fees vary (typically ~$100-$300 per team; CT fees set by state organizers)
aid: None

name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS) - Connecticut Region
eligibility: US high school students in grades 9-12 (US citizens or lawful permanent residents); students compete in the region of their school's address

notes: jshs.org announced 'JSHS has officially returned' for 2026-27; regional symposium windows Jan-Mar 2027 and National Symposium ~April 2027 with exact dates posted by individual regions in fall 2026. Requires an original research project (paper, abstract, poster, and ~12-min oral). Regional top-5 finalists advance; CT region previously continued as a state-only event during the suspension, so confirm the 2027 format on jshs.org.

name: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO)
eligibility: US high school students grades 9-12; US citizen or permanent resident required to advance past the Local Exam; under age 20 as of July 1 of the competition year
cost: Free (local exams typically free via school/ACS section; no national fee)
aid: None

Awards: top ~50 High Honors, ~190 Honors nationally. Prep: ACS official past exams and exam archive.

name: iGEM High School Competition
eligibility: High school competition: all student team members must be high school students as of March 31 of the competition year; team requires a PI (teacher/mentor) and institutional or community-lab affiliation

notes: 2026 cycle pattern (2027 dates expected similar Feb-Jun 2027): Early registration Feb 12, Regular Apr 2, Late Jun 4; team roster freeze mid-Sep; Grand Jamboree Nov 13-16, 2026 in Paris. Program fee paid in stages (Stage I registration EUR 4,950-5,950; Stage II finalization EUR 2,750). High school teams compete in one combined section. Deliverables include wiki, safety forms, and a project promotion video.

name: Genes in Space
eligibility: US students in grades 7-12 attending US public, private, or home schools; enter individually or in pairs with an adult sponsor; one submission per student per year

Awards: 5 Finalist, 5 Junior Scientist, 5 Constellation, 10 Honorable Mention. 2027 dates not yet announced - check genesinspace.org in late 2026.

aid: None

Judging emphasizes scientific merit (40%) plus creative ability.

name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
eligibility: Open to pre-college students worldwide; US students compete for national team selection; anyone can create a free usaco.org account
cost: Free

notes: 2025-26 season dates (2026-27 expected Dec 2026 / Jan 2027 / Feb 2027 / Mar 2027, announced ~mid-November on usaco.org): contests Jan 9-12, Jan 30-Feb 2, Feb 20-23, US Open Mar 28. Perfect scores earn instant in-contest promotion; otherwise division cutoffs apply. Prep: free past problems on usaco.org and the community usaco.guide.

name: DOE National Science Bowl (NSB)
eligibility: US high school teams of 4 students + 1 alternate + 1 teacher coach from the same school (grades 9-12); teams register for the regional designated for their school's location

Free practice questions available on the OSTI NSB site. ~10,000 students compete across 65 high-school regionals annually.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI) - MIT
eligibility: Current high school juniors with one year remaining before graduation (seniors not eligible); US citizens/permanent residents and international students from participating countries; must be at least 16 years old by July 1 of the program year

RSI Stanford (50 students, free) announced Aug 2026 with details to be released; both mirror the MIT model. Apply via cee.org.

name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
eligibility: Current high school juniors only (freshmen, sophomores, seniors not eligible); at least 15 and not yet 19 during all program dates; completed relevant coursework for credit (Biochemistry: biology + chemistry + strong algebra; Cell Biology: biology + algebra II; Bacterial Genomics: biology + algebra II)

notes: 2026 cycle: applications opened Dec 31, 2025; international deadline Jan 29, 2026; domestic deadline Feb 19, 2026. 2027 dates expected similar (opens ~Dec 31, 2026 / early Jan 2027; domestic deadline ~mid-Feb 2027 - confirm when posted). Programs run mid-June to late July. Standardized tests not considered for admission. Free to apply.

name: Jackson Laboratory Summer Student Program (SSP)
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors and undergraduate students; US citizens or lawful permanent residents; high-school applicants apply through the dedicated Bar Harbor application portal (2026 HS app: 'currently a high school senior')

aid: Fully funded for all admitted students (stipend + room, board, travel)

Highly selective: ~24-37 trainees from 500+ applicants. Students may not hold other jobs/classes during the program.

name: Anson L. Clark Scholar Program (Texas Tech)
eligibility: Highly qualified rising high school seniors and recent graduates; must be at least 17 years old by the program start date (no exceptions); 3 letters of recommendation (2 from teachers)

aid: None needed - fully funded for admitted students
notes: 2026 cycle: application deadline Feb 16, 2026; program ran Jun 21 - Aug 6, 2026. Expect a similar mid-February 2027 deadline. Application includes short essays, transcript, top-5 activities list, and 3 recommendations. Open to gifted students in nearly any academic area.

name: Simons Summer Research Program (Stony Brook)
eligibility: Current 11th graders (apply during junior year, attend summer before senior year); US citizens or permanent residents; at least 16 years old by program start; SCHOOL NOMINATION REQUIRED - each high school may nominate at most 2 students (no exceptions)
cost: Free - no tuition; stipend award presented at the closing poster symposium; participants arrange their own housing/commute
aid: Stipend award at program end; no tuition or fees
notes: 2026 cycle: school nominations due Jan 30, 2026; application deadline Feb 5, 2026; teacher recommendations Feb 13, 2026; decisions early April; program Jun 29 - Aug 7, 2026. Expect similar dates for 2027 (confirm when posted). Two teacher recommendations required (STEM preferred). Late/incomplete applications automatically disqualified.

eligibility: High school students in grades 11-12; at least 16 years old on or before July 4 of the program year (no exceptions); unweighted GPA of 95/100 (3.8/4.0); at least 3 of English, Chemistry, Math/Calculus, Physics, Biology (honors/AP a plus); standardized test scores (PSAT/SAT/ACT/Regents) at or above the 60th percentile
cost: $4,000 laboratory usage fee (does NOT include room/board); optional room-and-board package billed separately by Campus Residences (~$54+/night double); $50 registration fee
aid: None - the program explicitly states it cannot offer financial aid or scholarships

Requires 3 recommendation letters (one from a science teacher) and official transcript sent by the school.

name: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS, formerly TASP)
eligibility: High school sophomores and juniors (rising juniors and rising seniors); at least age 15 at program start and no older than 17 by program end

aid: Free for all students; additional aid for travel and replaced summer wages
notes: 2026 cycle: applications opened Oct 15, 2025, closed Dec 3, 2025; interviews Feb 2026; decisions March 2026; program Jun 21 - Jul 25, 2026. 2027 timeline per apply.tellurideassociation.org: applications available fall 2026, due winter 2026, 5 weeks June-July 2027 (exact deadline TBD). No grades; community living and democratic decision-making are central. Nominations are optional and do not affect chances.

name: Congressional App Challenge (2026)
eligibility: Middle or high school students at time of submission; compete in the district of residence or school; teams of up to 4 with at least half of members eligible in the competing district
cost: Free

notes: 2026 cycle: registration open since May/June 2026; apps due Oct 26, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET (submit source code + 2-min YouTube/Vimeo demo video). Register intent by Sept 30 recommended; districts must register by Sept 15, 2026 (verify his district on the site). Winners' apps are featured in the Capitol and on the CAC website.

name: NASA TechRise Student Challenge (2026-27)
eligibility: US public, private, or charter school students in grades 6-12 (incl. territories); teams of at least 4 students with a teacher/school employee as team lead
cost: Free

notes: 2026-27 challenge expected to open September 2026 (pre-registration at futureengineers.org/nasatechrise); 2025-26 entries were due Nov 3 with 60 winning teams selected (35 suborbital + 25 high-altitude balloon). 2026-27 flight vehicle is a high-altitude balloon; experiment build runs winter-spring, flights summer.

name: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI)
eligibility: Students residing in the US and attending high school physically in the US; must be in grade 9-11 (no current seniors or college students); must complete the online prerequisite course to be eligible to apply
cost: $2,400 for families with income above ~$200K; free for families below ~$200K (income verified after acceptance); housing not included
aid: Free tuition for qualifying family incomes; need-based support; housing not included for in-person courses
notes: For summer 2027: online prerequisite course registration opens ~December 2026 (self-register, no nomination needed); summer application sent to students completing the online course, due ~late March 2027 (2026 deadline was Mar 30; program ran Jul 6-Aug 2). Highly selective; courses include Serious Games with AI, Autonomous Systems, Quantum Computing, Cybersecurity, and more.

name: MIT THINK Scholars Program
eligibility: Full-time high school students (public, private, or homeschool) who are US residents during the academic year; apply individually or as a 2-person team; one proposal per academic year
cost: Free
aid: Up to $1,000 per project plus weekly MIT TechX mentorship and a fully-funded 4-day trip to MIT for finalists
notes: 2026-27 cycle: applications open November 1, 2026; due January 1, 2027; semifinalists announced ~Jan 30, finalists confirmed in February. Submit project title, abstract, research plan, budget, and references. Finalists implement the project over a semester with weekly mentor meetings.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) — Connecticut / NE District
eligibility: High school students grades 9-12 (ages 14-18); teams of up to ~25 students with adult mentors; join an existing CT school/community team or start one
cost: Free to join most school teams (team budgets of $5K-$10K+ are covered by team dues, sponsors, and CT state support); students' out-of-pocket cost is minimal
aid: CT Manufacturing Innovation Fund has committed ~$4.8M+ to CT robotics programs; FIRST offers $80M+ in scholarship opportunities; teams fundraise
notes: 2027 season game 'BIOCORE' kicks off January 9, 2027; team registration opens fall 2026 (kickoff-site selection Sept 24-Nov 17, 2026); district events run Feb-Apr 2027, CT State Championship in April, FIRST Championship in Houston. Also note FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC, grades 7-12) is available in CT for a lower-cost alternative. See nefirst.org/connecticut for CT specifics.

name: USA-North America AI Olympiad (USAAIO)
eligibility: US or Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or full-time middle/high school students studying in the US or Canada; must be under 20 on the first day of the international competition and not a full-time university student
cost: Free

notes: Three rounds: Round 1 (online), Round 2 (qualify via Round 1), USAAIO camp (qualify via Round 2); camp participants include US citizens/PRs plus international students at US schools, matching IOAI rules. 2026 IOAI was held Aug 2-8 in Astana, Kazakhstan with teams from 131 countries. Registration closes Jan 31, 2027 at 11:59 PM EST.

name: TSA Video Game Design (2026-27) — CT chapter
eligibility: TSA members in grades 9-12 (42 high-school events offered) via a school TSA chapter; teams of 1-6 for Video Game Design in CT
cost: TSA membership plus state/national conference registration (roughly $100-$300/year through his school chapter)
aid: None (nominal costs; many CT school districts fund TSA travel)

CT state conference typically held each spring (see ct-tsa.net for CT-specific rules); 2026 National Conference was in Washington, DC.

name: Games for Change (G4C) Student Challenge
eligibility: Young people ages 10-25 worldwide; US division split into Junior (10-13) and Senior (14-18) age groups
cost: Free

Unity discontinued its standalone Student Challenge and now supports youth game creation through G4C; past cycles welcomed digital games, tabletop games, character designs, and trailers addressing real-world challenges.

name: Global Game Jam Next (GGJ Next) 2027
eligibility: Students ages 10-18; participate at a local jam site (US/CT sites available; can also host one through a school)
cost: Free (most sites); some local sites may charge a nominal fee

notes: 2025-26 window ran Nov 15, 2025 - March 30, 2026 (aligned with the G4C Student Challenge); 2026-27 dates expected to open around November 2026 — watch globalgamejam.org/ggjnext for site announcements. Games must address global themes (e.g., food security, road safety, ecosystems).

name: GMTK Game Jam 2027
eligibility: Open to anyone aged 13+ worldwide (itch.io terms); individuals or teams of any size
cost: Free

notes: 2026 jam ran July 22-26 (theme 'Count Down', 10,562 entries); 2027 edition expected late July 2027 — follow gmtk.itch.io for the announcement. Theme is revealed at jam start; games must be made entirely within the 96-hour window.

eligibility: Open to all groups, entities, and individuals worldwide; projects must use Unreal Engine/UEFN or advance the real-time-3D ecosystem (including moving projects from other engines to Unreal)
cost: Free to apply

notes: 2026 Cycle 2: submission window June 29 - September 4, 2026 (closes 11:59 PM ET), review through Dec 4, notices Dec 7-11; next cycle expected early 2027. 2,100+ projects funded across 102 countries in 7 years. Applies to indie games, UEFN experiences, tools, open-source, and education content.

cost: Free
aid: Free to attend; travel/lodging not covered

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards

aid: National Medalists eligible for scholarships up to $12,500 (e.g., Portfolio Awards, Best-in-Grade $500, New York Life Award $2,500)

Writing categories include Critical Essay, Flash Fiction, Journalism, Poetry, Personal Essay & Memoir, Science Fiction & Fantasy, Short Story, and Novel Writing.

name: Bennington Young Writers Awards
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12 worldwide; one entry in one category (fiction, nonfiction, or poetry); entries must be reviewed and approved by a sponsoring teacher or mentor
cost: Free

notes: Opens Sept 1, 2026; deadline Nov 1, 2026. eligibility: High school sophomores and juniors at US-accredited schools (US, territories, Canada, American Schools Abroad); nominated by their school's English department

eligibility: High school students (including homeschooled) worldwide, plus college/university and graduate school divisions
